condition: Inguinal lymphadenopathy (suspected lymphoma) mimicking a hernia
summary: 46-year-old man referred as a "right inguinal hernia": firm, rubbery, non-reducible lumps with no cough impulse, night sweats and 6 kg weight loss. A lymph-node mass, not a hernia: ultrasound and biopsy, NICE NG12 suspected-lymphoma pathway; no hernia repair.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Lump in the right groin — referred as hernia
inputs.hpi: GP referral "right inguinal hernia". Lump present for 2 months, slowly enlarging, does not change with coughing or lying down, painless. Drenching night sweats for 6 weeks, lost 6 kg without trying, itchy skin. No foot or leg wounds.

exam.general: Well. Small left supraclavicular node palpable.
exam.abdomen: Soft. Right groin: matted, rubbery, non-tender lumps 3–4 cm below the inguinal ligament along the femoral vessels; irreducible, no cough impulse. Splenic tip palpable. Legs and feet normal skin.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Right inguinal lymphadenopathy with B symptoms — suspected lymphoma (not a hernia)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Not a hernia: matted irreducible inguinal nodes without cough impulse, B symptoms, splenomegaly and supraclavicular node — suspected lymphoma. Urgent USS groin and core/excision biopsy; FBC, LDH; haematology referral (suspected cancer pathway).

mustNotMiss.note: Non-reducible groin lumps without a cough impulse plus B symptoms: lymphadenopathy/lymphoma must be on the list.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3 = inguinal hernia, cholecystitis, GORD. PANE has no lymphadenopathy feature from the groin site and its only node disease is "Cervical Lymphadenopathy"; the symptom engine ranks lymphoma #1. PANE: unlisted features count at DEFAULT_SENSITIVITY 0.30 for every disease and there is no false-positive term, so high-prior abdominal diseases (cholecystitis 0.15, GORD 0.12, PUD 0.10; male inguinal hernia x5) outrank the organ-specific disease after a single non-abdominal feature.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Model P(feature | not disease) or use a low default sensitivity (e.g. <=0.05) for features outside a disease's system; restrict the candidate set by the presenting system (breast / neck / groin).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No groin ultrasound or node biopsy is proposed; the confirmed ICD R59.1 has no protocol (R59.9 → cervical lymphadenopathy only).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Map R59.x to a generic lymphadenopathy protocol (USS, FBC/LDH, core/excision biopsy, NG12 referral) regardless of site.

mustExclude.note: The referral label ("hernia") must not drive a hernia repair plan once the examination says lymph nodes.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Assessment ManagementPanel follows the PANE top disease (≥0.20), which is the inguinal hernia because the only groin CC template is "Inguinal / groin hernia" and site "groin" maps to groin_swelling; the surgeon's confirmed diagnosis (ICD) is not used for the panel while PANE is ≥0.20. The panel shows "Elective: Lichtenstein mesh herniorrhaphy … TEP/TAPP" and the TAPP prompt fires from the CC template name.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Let the confirmed working diagnosis (ICD / paneDiseaseId) override the PANE top for the ManagementPanel, and add a neutral "Groin lump" CC template.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
guideline.section: Site-specific recommendations: breast cancer (age ≥30 unexplained lump; ≥50 unilateral nipple discharge/retraction; skin changes; men ≥50 subareolar mass), haematological cancers (unexplained lymphadenopathy), head and neck (unexplained thyroid lump)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (updated).

guideline.name: HerniaSurge — International guidelines for groin hernia management
guideline.section: Diagnosis (clinical examination, ultrasound for uncertain swellings); watchful waiting in minimally symptomatic men; mesh repair (Lichtenstein, TEP/TAPP); groin hernia in women; femoral hernia; emergency repair
guideline.citation: HerniaSurge Group. International guidelines for groin hernia management. Hernia. 2018;22:1–165.

rationale: Groin mimic. The referral and the only groin CC template both say "hernia"; the examination and B symptoms say lymph nodes. Tests anchoring: the plan and differential must follow the findings, not the referral label.
